description:
List available models.

The Models API response can be used to determine which models are available for use in the API. More recently released models are listed first.

parameters.description: ID of the object to use as a cursor for pagination. When provided, returns the page of results immediately before this object.
parameters.name: before_id

schema.description: ID of the object to use as a cursor for pagination. When provided, returns the page of results immediately before this object.
schema.title: Before Id

parameters.description: ID of the object to use as a cursor for pagination. When provided, returns the page of results immediately after this object.
parameters.name: after_id

schema.description: ID of the object to use as a cursor for pagination. When provided, returns the page of results immediately after this object.
schema.title: After Id

parameters.description:
Number of items to return per page.

Defaults to `20`. Ranges from `1` to `1000`.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description:

schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: Filter the list to models in any of the given lifecycle stages (`active`, `deprecated`, or `retired`). Up to 3 values. When omitted, the list contains the `active` and `deprecated` models; `retired` models appear only when `retired` is requested explicitly.
parameters.name: lifecycle[]

schema.description: Filter the list to models in any of the given lifecycle stages (`active`, `deprecated`, or `retired`). Up to 3 values. When omitted, the list contains the `active` and `deprecated` models; `retired` models appear only when `retired` is requested explicitly.
schema.title: Lifecycle[]

Optional header to select the Workspace for this request. The value is a Workspace ID (for example, `wrkspc_011CZkZaBF1tNoB5wlCeusgy`).

Only needed for credentials that can act on more than one Workspace. A credential that belongs to a specific Workspace may omit it; if sent, it must match that Workspace.

details.description: Machine-readable detail about the cause of the error. `error_code` names the cause; branch on it rather than on `message`. Absent when the error has no code. Treat an unrecognized `error_code` as the bare `type`.
details.title: Details

400.description: Invalid argument - The client specified an invalid argument

401.description: Unauthenticated - The request does not have valid authentication credentials

403.description: Permission denied - The caller does not have permission to execute the specified operation

404.description: Not found - Some requested entity was not found

408.description: Deadline exceeded - The deadline expired before the operation could complete

409.description: Aborted - The operation was aborted due to concurrency issue

412.description: Failed precondition - Operation was rejected because the system is not in required state

413.description: Out of range - Operation was attempted past the valid range

429.description: Resource exhausted - Some resource has been exhausted (rate limiting)

431.description: Request header fields too large - Request metadata was too large

499.description: Cancelled - The operation was cancelled by the client

501.description: Unimplemented - The operation is not implemented or supported

503.description: Unavailable - The service is currently unavailable

504.description: Deadline exceeded - Upstream service did not respond in time

529.description: Overloaded - The service is temporarily overloaded

first_id.description: First ID in the `data` list. Can be used as the `before_id` for the previous page.
first_id.title: First Id

has_more.description: Indicates if there are more results in the requested page direction.

last_id.title: Last Id

BetaClaudeCodeKeyCreatorNotMemberErrorDe.title: ClaudeCodeKeyCreatorNotMemberErrorDetails

BetaOrganizationOnHoldErrorDetails.title: OrganizationOnHoldErrorDetails

allowed_fallback_models.description: Model IDs this model accepts as `fallbacks[i].model` on the Messages API. An empty list means the `fallbacks` parameter is not supported for this model as primary.
allowed_fallback_models.title: Allowed Fallback Models

capabilities.description: Object mapping capability names to their support details. Keys are always present for all known capabilities.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 datetime string representing the time at which the model was released. May be set to an epoch value if the release date is unknown.
created_at.title: Created At

deprecated_at.description: RFC 3339 datetime string representing the time of the model's most recent deprecation. Populated for `deprecated` and `retired` models; `null` while the model is `active`.
deprecated_at.title: Deprecated At

display_name.description: A human-readable name for the model.
display_name.title: Display Name

lifecycle.description:
The model's current lifecycle stage.

- `active`: The model is available for use, open to new adopters, and not scheduled for retirement.
- `deprecated`: The model remains callable for organizations with existing access, but is headed for retirement and closed to new adopters.
- `retired`: The model is no longer available for use; inference requests naming it fail. It remains in the catalogue as the historical record of its retirement.
lifecycle.title: Lifecycle

line.description: The model line this model belongs to, such as `opus` for both Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6. More lines may be added. `null` when the model belongs to no line; do not infer a line from the `id`.

max_input_tokens.description: Maximum input context window size in tokens for this model.
max_input_tokens.title: Max Input Tokens

max_tokens.description: Maximum value for the `max_tokens` parameter when using this model.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

retires_at.description: RFC 3339 datetime string representing the model's currently scheduled retirement date. The schedule can be revised until retirement occurs; `null` while the model is `active` or while no retirement is scheduled. A past date on a `deprecated` model means retirement is overdue, not that it has occurred: `lifecycle` is the retirement signal.
retires_at.title: Retires At

type.description:
Object type.

For Models, this is always `"model"`.
type.title: Type

batch.description: Whether the model supports the Batch API.

citations.description: Whether the model supports citation generation.

code_execution.description: Whether code that the model runs in the code execution tool can call the request's other tools, as in programmatic tool calling and dynamic filtering for web search and web fetch. Support for the code execution tool itself is in `server_tools.code_execution`.

compaction.description: Server-side compaction support (the top-level `compaction` parameter) and the accepted `compaction.type` values.

context_management.description: Context management support and available strategies.

image_input.description: Whether the model accepts image content blocks.

pdf_input.description: Whether the model accepts PDF content blocks.

server_tools.description: Whether this model supports the web search and code execution server tools. `supported` is true when the model supports at least one of the tools. A supported tool can still be rejected for your organization, for example when an admin has turned web search off.

structured_outputs.description: Whether the model supports structured output / JSON mode / strict tool schemas.

thinking.description: Thinking capability and supported type configurations.

BetaModelLine.description: A Claude model line, such as `opus` or `sonnet`. More lines may be added as new values.
BetaModelLine.title: ModelLine

BetaThinkingTypes.description: Which `thinking.type` values the model accepts on requests. Read each key on its own: for example, `enabled` can be false while `disabled` is true.

adaptive.description: Whether the model accepts thinking with type 'adaptive' (the model decides whether and how much to think).

between_tools.description: Whether the model accepts thinking with type 'between_tools' (thinking turned off, and any short progress updates the model writes between tool calls come back as thinking blocks). False exactly when a request that sends it gets a 400 from this model. A request that sends 'between_tools' can still be rejected for another reason, such as an effort level the model does not allow with thinking off.

disabled.description: Whether the model accepts thinking with type 'disabled' (thinking turned off). False exactly when a request that sends it gets a 400 from this model. True on a model that does not support thinking. A request that sends 'disabled' can still be rejected for another reason, such as an effort level the model does not allow with thinking off.

enabled.description: Whether the model accepts thinking with type 'enabled' (extended thinking with a caller-set `budget_tokens`).

BetaThinkingTypes.title: ThinkingTypes
